206975307.description:
Hello! I'm Beau! I'm a very sweet boy with a unique feature. I'm a tripod! But don't let that fool you, I'm even more playful as ever! I love to go on walks and be outside. I even enjoy the water! I am house and kennel trained, and I love to hang out with the other dogs in my foster home. Sometimes we will play, but we all like to relax together too! While I get along with the dogs in my foster home, I do need slower intros with other dogs to help me feel comfortable. I am not a fan of hissing cats, so a home without cats would be best.

I enjoy puzzle toys and dog safe chews.  While I am a playful and adventerous boy, I also like to snuggle sometimes. Apartment life is too overwhelming for me, so I need a house, preferably with a fenced in yard, to call my forever home. However, the fenced in yard is not a dealbreaker since I enjoy going on walks.

I do have anxiety and allergies, so I take meds for them. But don't worry, I do really well taking them!

Are you my perfect match?

211913939.description:
Hi, I’m Pepper! 🐾

I’m an 8 ½ year-old bundle of love with the biggest heart and so much love to give! My foster family says I’m a special girl with a goofy personality, a playful spirit, and a heart that is truly one of a kind.

I may need a little extra patience and understanding when getting to know new people and navigating the world around me. New experiences and unfamiliar dogs can sometimes feel overwhelming, so I’m looking for someone who understands that building trust is a process. I may not open my heart overnight, but when I do, you’ll have a friend who loves with her whole heart. Once I trust you, you’ll get to see the real Pepper - the silly, affectionate, playful girl who loves to snuggle, give kisses, lean in for affection, and make you laugh. I have so much personality packed into this big body, and I truly believe I’m a lap dog! My favorite things include toys, treats, naps, and spending time with my people. And yes, my adorable snoring is just one of my many charms!

I currently live with another female dog, and we have a wonderful relationship. We love to play and chase each other, and she is a very special part of my world. While I do well with my resident dog, I have found that I’m most comfortable in a home where I don’t have to share my people or space with other dogs. I would likely thrive as the only dog in the home, where I can soak up all the love and attention. I’m looking for a quieter home with a patient, compassionate person or family who understands my needs and will give me the time and support I deserve. A female-led home would be a wonderful fit for me, and I would do best without children. I’m hoping for someone who sees the beauty in taking things slowly and understands that the most meaningful relationships are built one day at a time.

My foster family has watched me come so far. I’m learning that the world can be a wonderful place and that new experiences don’t always have to be scary. Every little bit of progress makes us so proud, and we know there is still so much happiness ahead of me. I’m a playful, loving girl who has so much more to discover. I may need someone willing to be patient, but I promise that the love I give in return is worth every moment. Once you become my person, you’ll have a loyal companion who wants nothing more than to be by your side. My foster family loves me dearly, and while saying goodbye will be incredibly difficult, they know there is someone out there who will see just how extraordinary I am.

I’m not looking for a perfect home. I’m looking for the right home - a home with patience, understanding, and a whole lot of heart. If you’re willing to give me the time I need to feel safe and loved, I’ll show you just how much love this big-hearted girl has to give ❤️

212359159.description:
Sweet Maple has been with us since she was 4-weeks-old. She came in with her mom (pictured with her) and 6 siblings, who have all be long since adopted. For some reason Maple sits and waits.

She started out going to the same events as her siblings, and got no interest. She was posted online everywhere, and got no interest.

We stopped attending events due to Maple being very shut down at them. We tried again once she was old enough to be on leash and outdoor events started; however, she was still very anxious and had a really hard time warming up to people.

Maple at home is an entirely different story. She warms up to people so fast, especially if you have treats, and a doggie friend for her to play with.

Maple is a very cautious girl, around people and will require another dog in the home for her to buddy up with.  She is great with all sizes of dogs, and she loves cats as well. She does very well with kids too!  She loves to be chased by them in the yard. Her favorite game is "chase me." She does okay on a leash, but would definitely do much better, and adjust so much easier, to a home with a fenced in yard. She is also fairly vocal when she hears noises, so she would not do well in an apartment  or other living space with shared walls.

At this point I could write a book about this sweet little devil, but I will wrap it but by saying she has some quirks and she will need to be on medication the rest of her life for urinary incontinence, but you won't find a better dog that can make you feel every emotion in one day, lol.

We truly love her and we know her perfect family will find her.

212449123.description:
Meet Jillian! If you are looking for a pup with a ton of personality and a lot of love, then Jillian is your girl.

With big amber eyes and a uniquely painted coat, Jillian is a showstopper. She loves all humans she meets and is a huge sweetheart, but does need continued boundary work as she thinks the best way to let others know she is a fan is to get right up into their personal space! However, she is smart and has picked up on cues and commands very quickly.

Jillian is crate trained and has done well being crated for longer periods of time while her foster is at work. When crated, she tends to do better in a high-traffic area so she can observe what is going on around her and not miss out. While Jillian has not been left alone in the house outside the crate for long periods of time, during shorter bouts, she has done really well and usually just ends up lounging in the living room or sunroom.

Jillian is also potty-trained. She has cleared our 3-foot fence to go after squirrels so is currently on a lead even with a fenced-in backyard. As an almost 2-year-old, Jillian still has a lot of youthful energy and looks forward to going for her walk first thing in the morning. And while she has made a lot of progress over the last few months, Jillian does have a high prey drive and exhibits some excitable reactivity as a result.

Jillian does express high interest in playing with other dogs but will require monitoring as she does not always appropriately read social cues. Slow introductions are best for her.

In just a short amount of time, Jillian has learned both the verbal and nonverbal signals for “sit”, “wait”, “hands in”, “stay” and “lie down”. She transports well and loves her weekly outdoor adventures at Fort Snelling.

Overall, Jillian's ideal home is with an active family or person who is patient, is in a house (she does have a heavy bark!) with a high fenced-in yard. If you are ready for a lively spirit, funny personality, and unconditional companionship - look no further than Jillian!

212549943.description:
Meet Buttercup!

Buttercup is a sweet, gentle pup who can be a little shy and reserved when meeting new people, but once she feels safe she becomes very loving and loyal to her people.

Buttercup has low-to-moderate energy and enjoys both playtime and cuddles. She loves playing fetch and will happily bring the ball back so you can throw it again. She’s also extremely treat and food motivated, which makes training fun and rewarding. Belly rubs, snacks, and greeting her people when they come home are some of her favorite things.

She is good with other dogs, but can be reactive when she sees them from a distance and does best with slow introductions. Buttercup doesn’t need another dog in the home, but a calm, friendly dog could help build her confidence.

Buttercup is afraid of men and will need a patient home that allows her time to warm up. Because she isn’t familiar with toddlers, she would do best with older children. She sleeps well in her crate at night and learned potty training quickly.

Buttercup cannot live with cats.

She’s a very sweet, cuddly girl who has clearly had a difficult past and just needs a patient family who will give her the love and security she deserves.

213112143.description:
Hi, I'm Norman!

My foster mom scooped me up when she heard how I came into rescue. I was hanging around a hospital trying to find snacks and minding my own business when some bigger dogs decided I wasn't welcome. Thankfully, a kind woman who worked there stepped in to help, and the rest is history!

I've been living with my foster family since February, and I just celebrated my first birthday in September. My foster mom says I've grown up a lot, but personally, I think I've only become more awesome.

If you're looking for a couch potato, keep scrolling. If you're looking for a dog who wakes up every morning ready to seize the day, chase a ball, wrestle a friend, go for a hike, and then do it all over again... we should talk. I'm a high-energy guy with a zest for life and absolutely zero interest in wasting a perfectly good day lying around.

Because I'm still young and enthusiastic about literally everything, I'll need a family that can keep me active and provide consistent rules and boundaries. I do best when I know what's expected of me. Think of me as an athlete with a big heart and occasionally questionable decision-making skills.

Speaking of my heart... I LOVE people. I want to know what you're doing, where you're going, whether you're eating snacks, and if I can help. (Spoiler: I probably can't help, but I'd still like to be involved.) I thrive on human attention and am always happy to hand out cuddles after I've burned off some energy.

I generally get along well with other dogs and love having canine friends. My foster mom says I can be a little rude sometimes. I prefer to think of myself as extremely enthusiastic about making friends immediately. Personal space is a concept I'm still studying.

I also have a very important hobby: squirrel surveillance. When I'm outside, I patrol the yard to make sure those sneaky little creatures aren't up to anything. When I'm inside, I can often be found sitting at the window carefully monitoring squirrel activity and providing updates to my foster family. So far, I have not caught a squirrel, but I remain committed to the mission.

I'm crate trained and eat and sleep in my crate. Sometimes I even choose to hang out in there all by myself, which makes my foster mom act like I've discovered quantum physics.

I also happen to be very food motivated. Want me to learn something? Snacks. Need my attention? Snacks. Trying to win my heart? You guessed it... snacks.

I do well with kids, but because I'm such an energetic dude, I'd be happiest in a home with older children who can handle my excitement and playful personality.

So if you're active, like adventures, appreciate a dog with a sense of humor, and don't mind being loved enthusiastically, I might just be your perfect match.

Love,

Norman 🐾

I’m pretty good with cats, but I’m still learning not to chase them when they run. They have a tiny baby kitty that they bottle fed & that kitten is my best friend!

I like to pull when I’m excited, but I’m still a puppy so they tell me it’s okay & we will keep working on that.

I really love being outside & exploring the big yard, but I also am very happy to just snuggle up & relax. I will happily go find a toy or bone in the box to entertain myself too. Being adorable really is hard work!

• My Origin Story: Rescued from under an abandoned shed in Arkansas with my two

brothers.

• My Personality: Sassy, spunky, brave, and completely fearless.

• My Favorite Things: Running outdoors, playing with other dogs, making kid friends, and

getting treats.

From Humble Beginnings to Big Adventures:

My brothers and I started out under an abandoned shed in Arkansas, but I was born to explore! I am the ultimate adventurer. If my brothers are hesitant about going somewhere new, I just charge right right in to show them how it's done. I love the great outdoors and am very good at staying close to my foster parents when I'm off-leash. There is just too much fun stuff to see!

Small Package, Big Personality:

People say I am spunky and sassy. I also have zero problems voicing my thoughts, opinions, and demands—I am highly communicative! I am also completely fearless. If someone or something big comes into "my space," I will absolutely question their existence at first. But don't worry! As soon as I know you, it is nothing but non-stop butt wiggles and sweet puppy kisses.

Smart Girl Status:

I am learning how to be the best dog ever, and I'm progressing fast:

• Potty Training: I am doing amazing! I prefer to go outdoors. When I'm inside, I use my potty

pads like a pro. The only time I have an accident is when I get super tired.

• Basic Commands: I am practicing my manners and learning commands. My absolute

favorite part of school is getting the treats!

My Dream Family:

I absolutely love other dogs and I love kids! My perfect forever home will have plenty of outdoor

playtime, some fun furry or human siblings, and a family who appreciates a brave girl with a lot of look-at-me attitude.

214265511.description:
Tito is suspected to have come to us from a hoarding situation after potentially being bred / a "stud." After a difficult start to life, he is understandably guarded and defensive, and he will need a patient, understanding adopter who is willing to let him build trust at his own pace.

Tito is smart, sassy, independent, and incredibly curious. He’s a bit like a “wisp of smoke”—quick, elusive, and determined to keep all four paws on the ground! He isn’t comfortable being picked up yet, but we’re making progress every day.

He has especially begun to trust his foster mom, choosing to curl up beside her in her recliner. Because of this, we suspect Tito may be more comfortable with women and may need extra time to feel safe around men. He is also gradually warming up to his teenage foster grandsons, showing us that his circle of trust can grow with patience and consistency.

Tito appears to have had little-to-no training before coming into rescue. He is currently pee-pad trained and sleeps quite a bit.

For now, Tito is not a fan of other dogs. He reacts strongly toward the resident dog, so they are kept separated. He is also a significant flight risk and has managed to escape harnesses and take off, so his adopter will need to be extremely careful and use secure, escape-proof equipment and management.

Tito is not going to be an “easy” dog, but he is a worthwhile one. His adopter will need to be committed to giving him time, structure, patience, and plenty of opportunities to learn that the world can be a safe place. In return, they’ll get a smart, savvy, energetic little companion.

Tito is looking for someone who understands that trust isn't given overnight—it’s earned one tiny step at a time. And with Tito, those tiny steps are incredibly rewarding.

214344991.description:
Lorraine is a beautiful, fun loving youngster who remains fearful of unfamiliar sounds, and sudden movements. She can be a rascal when she feels comfortable and confident as far as checking out what’s on the kitchen counter that may be tasty.

She walks well on a leash as long as her person is alert for squirrels!!

She loves to sit patiently and watch out the window for squirrels. She is not a barker even with those hound dog ears.

Lorraine would do best with another dog in the family to help her feel safe and show her the ropes, and she would benefit from having a fenced in backyard. She enjoys playing chase with any dog willing to run fast, and she likes to wrestle (very quietly) with the foster family’s cattle dog.

She’s not been around cats or young kids.  Pretty sure she would appreciate the more predictable movements of adolescents.

Lorraine can be quite willful when it comes to going in her crate, or putting on her collar to go for a walk. She’s very food motivated so she would thrive in a beginning level obedience class.

She’s a beautiful dog looking for someone who works from home so she doesn’t have to spend a great deal of time in her crate. She sleeps quietly on her own bed next to her foster parents.

Lorraine has faced a truckload of traumas and daunting challenges in her short life. She’s waiting for the right person or family to envelope her with care, structure, and love to help her become her best self. She’s soooo worth the investment of time and energy!

214354283.description:
Looking for a spunky, energetic kitten?! Cari is your girl!

When she first arrived, she was pretty sick, but after a quick visit to the vet and the necessary meds, Cari was feeling better almost immediately! It wasn't long before her brave, energetic personality really began to shine! You may notice her right eye looks a little different. This is a temporary effect of the severe upper respiratory infection she had when she arrived in our care, but it should resolve on its own now that Cari has finished her meds and is feeling like a healthy kitten again!

Cari is a very playful and social girl. She loves being around people and even better if they are up for a play session! She is obsessed with her crinkle ball, but can make a toy out of literally anything... whether you like it or not :) This includes fingers and toes... but we are working on redirecting her with actual toys when that happens! For this reason, older children may be a better fit for her. She has even found dog toys to be equally as fun as cat toys! Cari has been living with 3 dogs and 3 cats. She LOVES to play with one of our foster dogs. They have become really great friends! She even likes to nap near him. So safe to say she is dog friendly! She has been very hesitant about meeting the resident cats, but with time and proper introductions, I think she could do well with a friendly, playful feline companion.

Cari plays to her heart's content, which also means she works up quite an appetite! Cari is a huge fan of meal time and doesn't appear to be picky! She loves it all! So no fighting with this one when it comes to choosing what's for dinner. That's a huge win in our book! She also does really well with being picked up and carried. And when she wants to be put down, she will certainly let you know with her  big girl meow! Once and awhile, mainly at bedtime, she will curl up and snuggle with us humans for a little bit which is a real treat.

Cari is the perfect mix of sweet & spunky- and will certainly keep you laughing every day with her crazy, playful antics!

Joel gets along great with the 10-year-old human who lives in his foster home, and is always happy to see her. The dog in his foster home is not as excited as Joel is to play, so they haven't spent a ton of time together. I think Joel would be fine as a solo pet or with another dog in the home who matches his energy and enjoys playing. He seems to have a stronger prey drive, so living with a cat may be difficult.

Joel is the sweetest boy! He is ready to pour all of his love into whoever is lucky enough to adopt him.

211013418.description:
Yuki is a gentle and sweet girl. She loves to leap into the chair to snuggle with her favorite person. She’s got super soft fur that she hopes will get scratched while she’s there.

She is a smart pup. She can sit on command and is beginning to stay. She loves 1:1 training time, complete with treats.

In her previous home, she learned to ring a bell when she wanted to go outside. (She is potty trained.)

She sleeps overnight in a crate and can spend several hours a day in a crate (although she may be fine free roaming a portion of the house once she has adjusted.) She has not chewed on anything besides her toys while she’s been with us.

Yuki can be hesitant in a new environment and will benefit from a patient family that will allow her to get comfortable at her own pace. A calm and predictable home with kids 12 and up would be best for her. Chaos can be overwhelming to her.

A slow, safe introduction to a new pet sibling will be important for Yuki.

Yuki loves our fenced backyard. She happily runs and wrestles with the resident dog - as long as it’s not raining. She’s a bit particular about the weather.

She is an enthusiastic walker! She pulls a bit to begin with. She wants to get all the smells in, but she will settle down after a short time. Yuki likes seeing other dogs on walks and will pull to greet them.

At playtime, squeaky tennis balls are her favorite. Plush toys are a good back-up. She does need a bit of practice with sharing toys - sometimes she likes to steal toys away from other dogs.

Yuki really enjoys chasing cats, so a cat-free home is probably a necessity.

Though she has her playful and adventurous side, sitting beside a person is her favorite way to wrap up the day. If you are looking for the ultimate companion, Yuki is your girl. Adventure? She’s in! Couch snuggles? Absolutely!

Could you be her person? Apply and make it official!

Rescued from a South Dakota reservation with her three puppies, Starbies is one very special girl—and an absolutely amazing mama. She is patient, gentle, and calm, with a sweet soul that makes you want to give her the whole world.

Starbies loves the freedom of being outdoors and would happily join you on your adventures, but she is just as content to curl up and lounge quietly when it’s time to relax. Whether you’re heading out for the day or settling in for a cozy night of movies, Starbies is ready to be your sweetest sidekick.

And did we mention she is quiet? Starbies is not a barker, and honestly, I’m not sure I’ve even heard her make a peep! She is wonderful in her kennel, keeps it clean, and has not had a single accident in her foster home. What a good girl!

Starbies can be a little leery when meeting someone for the first time, but it doesn’t take long for her to figure out that you’re one of the good ones. Once she warms up, be prepared for all the kisses you’re willing to accept!

She also has a strong prey drive and LOVES to run and play. She is very active, but when she gets her exercise she does enjoy cuddling up for a good nap.

Now that her puppies are taken care of, it’s Mama Starbies’ turn to find the loving home she deserves—a person or family who will show her what being loved truly feels like.

Could Starbies be your perfect match? If you haven’t had the pleasure of meeting this sweet girl yet, fill out an adoption application and schedule your meet and greet. Starbies is patiently waiting for her forever family—and we think they’re going to be very lucky to find each other.

214131108.description:
Meyer is a handsome, smart, and loving pup with a mighty brave heart and a big personality. He's a medium-sized guy with a bit of terrier tenacity, but he's also alert, trainable, and eager to learn. He's very snuggly, sleeps at the foot of the bed (usually right on your feet), and is completely devoted to his people.

Meyer is athletic and energetic, with a nice off-switch. He can entertain himself with toys or settle into a cozy spot with a bone. He's house-trained, not a chewer or excessive barker, though he'll definitely alert you to strange noises! He loves car rides to farmers markets, restaurants, and breweries, and enjoys swimming, hiking, and dog parks. Water is his happy place.

Meyer likes other dogs and is working on his play manners. He plays rough but takes verbal correction well. He can be persistent, so an assertive medium or large dog may be a better match. He'd also do wonderfully as a solo dog, since he loves his people so much.

Meyer is good with kids, though he may ankle nip when they run, so he'll do best with kids who can learn to be calm around him. He's good with dog-savvy cats, but he'll want to play and is always ready to chase if a cat runs.

If you're looking for a best friend who will bring joy, laughter, and plenty of snuggles to your life, Meyer may be the perfect match!

Nala is a puppy and just beginning to learn what it means to have a stable, loving home.

She arrived after a long travel day and was understandably unsure at first. A bath helped her settle, and she quickly latched onto her foster dad — following him around at his heels and seeking that close human connection. She’s already come a long way in just a few days. Nala comes when called, has that classic awkward puppy run (think lanky, goofy Scooby-Doo energy), and has slept through the night for three nights in a row. She kennels well and is starting to pick up basic manners, including learning “down” to help with counter-surfing.

In her foster home, she’s getting consistent nutrition and is already gaining confidence. House training is coming along in strides when there aren’t too many distractions — she’s still learning the household routine. At first, the bigger dogs were a little overwhelming for her, but she has warmed up quickly and now loves to play with our Doberman Alexis, Australian Shepherd/Husky mix Bell, and Corgi mix Pips. How she does with cats or other animals is still unknown.

Nala is a great puppy with a gentle, people-oriented nature and a playful, slightly goofy personality. She thrives on attention and consistency, and with a little more time to grow into her confidence, she’s going to make a wonderful companion.

While her life started in a heartbreaking, negligent situation where she was found starving and malnourished, those dark days are far behind her. Here is a quick look at what makes Cleopatra the perfect addition to the right home:

• Dog & Cat Friendly: She absolutely loves the company of other dogs and gets along wonderfully with cats, making her a great fit for a multi-pet household.

• Medium Energy Level: She is the perfect balance of fun and chill. She enjoys going out on adventures, exploring the neighborhood, and playing, but she is just as content to spend the afternoon snuggling on the couch.

• Loyal & Attentive: Because of her rough start in life, Cleo forms an incredibly strong bond with her people. She likes to know her owner is close by and thrives with an attentive adopter who will make her feel safe, secure, and loved.

Cleopatra is fully vetted, healthy, and patiently waiting for the family who will promise to never let her feel hungry or unloved ever again.

214567711.description:
Hello! I’m Petey Wheatie and I am an extra special girl looking for an extra special forever home.

In late September, I had a vet appointment and found that my glaucoma was so severe, and causing me so much pain, that both my eyes needed to be removed. I also had much needed dental work done to remove several infected teeth. I am no longer in pain, but it’s been quite an adjustment losing my sight.

While I couldn’t see well before, the complete loss of my vision has been a big adjustment. I am still a very happy girl who loves people and I especially love the quiet safety of my foster mom’s lap while she works.

While I currently live with dogs and a cat, I am easily startled by movement and noise, and can be territorial with my favorite spots, and would do best as an only dog/animal in a home without children and or a lot activity.

True to my breed, I am a vocal girl and like to communicate when I am excited, wanting attention, lonely, or feeling protective.

I much prefer to be with people and would be a great companion for a retired person or a home where my parent/s are home more than away.

I am reliably house trained, love treats, cuddling, burrowing under covers, am a very good sleeper, and am very excited by the short walks I’ve been able to take since my recovery.

Because I’m such a special girl, I will need a special home where my parent(s) are patient, willing to help me navigate my world, and are willing to make my immediate environment safe and accessible for me. If that sounds like you, apply today!

I’m a gentle, sweet boy who’s still learning that the world isn’t such a scary place! I can be a little shy at first, but once I start feeling comfortable, you’ll see just how much I love my people. A few things you should know about me:

- I’m crate-trained!

- I adore toddlers and have a sweet, gentle nature around little humans!

- I enjoy cats!

I’m still figuring out my feelings about other dogs, so I’ll need slow, proper introductions and a family willing to give me time to adjust.

I’m still learning how to navigate this big world, and sometimes I’m not quite sure what to make of everything around me. But with a little love, consistency, and encouragement, I know I can blossom into the most amazing companion.

I’m not looking for someone to make me perfect overnight. I’m looking for someone who will see my potential, celebrate my little victories, and love me through the moments when I need a little extra reassurance.

Could you be the person who helps me discover just how wonderful life can be?

Love, Prongs 🐾

214806465.description:
Hi, I’m Pinto Bean. Don’t let the name fool you—I’m not staying bean-sized for long. My fur really is as soft as it looks. My foster mom pets me and says I feel just like a downy chick!

The world is pretty much my favorite thing EVER. I’m naturally curious, super brave, and ready to check out every new sound, room, or backyard adventure.

Here’s what you should know about me:

Kids are my absolute favorites. I love everyone, but when little humans walk in the room, my whole tail takes over. I’m gentle, sweet, and thrilled to be their shadow.

I learned how to ask to go out! I’m almost totally house-trained. Whenever I need to potty, I just trot over and give the sliding glass door a little tap with my paw.

Fetch is life. Grab a ball, throw it, and I’m on it. I’ll bring it right back, or if you prefer a good game of tug, I’m fully down for that too.

I’m still learning my puppy manners. When I get excited, I sometimes forget fingers aren't toys, but a quick reminder or a crinkle toy swap gets me right back on track.

If it were up to me, I’d run nonstop forever! I want to see everything, sniff everything, and play at full throttle. Except apparently my engine has a shut-off switch I didn't know about. One minute I’m flying across the room, and the next—clunk—the battery unplugs, and I melt right into your lap like a ridiculously soft weighted blanket. Foster mom says all that adventuring requires “beauty sleep” (as if I’m not already gorgeous), but honestly, I think her lap is a pretty great spot to nap. And at bedtime, I head straight into my crate next to the bed and sleep quietly until morning.

If your home has room for a happy, ridiculously soft shadow who loves playing in the yard and snoozing on your feet, send in an application—I'm ready for my forever family!

Sir Oscar is quite certain he was born in the wrong century. A feline of refined tastes and discerning company, he expects to be treated with the utmost dignity. While he might not wear a physical crown upon his head, make no mistake—there is one firmly planted in his mind.

For the humans choosing to audition to serve him, His Majesty has laid out the following absolute requirements for his new kingdom:

-Oscar has decreed that no kittens shall be present in his home, there is no room for that sort of nonsense and personal space intrusion. Other feline courtiers may abide if they do not mind his rule and space, which may include occasional hissing during the introduction period. 

-Dogs are an unknown species at this time and Oscar has no official comment about them at this time. 

As far as the peasants bringing him wet food daily, let it be known that he will seek out your attention and expect little return of touching until he has settled into his new kingdom. Head nuzzles and quick back scratches are acceptable right away. He spicily thanks you in advance for reading his full decree. 

Sir Oscar would like noted that his unique shortened tail is for reasons unknown.

making great progress with cats. While he's still a little cautious around them, he's becoming more comfortable and confident every day.

For such a young dog, Dutch has already accomplished a lot. He:

- Walks nicely on a leash

- Sits when asked (most of the time!)

- Is kennel trained

- Is nearly potty trained

Dutch has all the ingredients of an incredible  family dog: a gentle heart, a playful spirit, and a deep love for his people. All that is missing is a forever home where he can continue to grow, learn, and be loved.

Dutch is hoping for a family that enjoys both adventure and downtime, a family that will toss a toy, share a couch, and never pass up a good snuggle. If that sounds like you, Dutch is ready to be your loyal companion for life.

Hi, I'm Grogu! I can't believe it's already been 3 weeks since I was taken into a safe space. Oh my goodness, my foster mom is so proud of how far I've come so quickly!

When I arrived at her house, I couldn't contain myself, I had no focus, needed to check everything out 50 times just to make sure nothing was going to jump out and get me, didn't know my own name, had no idea what to do when she talked to me, and just wanted to eat everything as fast as possible! But I knew I wanted to be as close as possible to these people who were being so nice to me. Pets and snuggles are my favorite thing!!! On top of that, there are friends for me to play with! And the cats are pretty cool, but I just let them do their thing, because they don't want to play.

I have a lot of terrier energy in me, but you are my main focus now, and I absolutely love watching the TV, too. My fosters figured out that I pay attention really well when I hear my name and a request in a calm, melodic voice. They taught me that if I do things they ask that I get even more attention and a tiny treat. I will sit, lay down, wait (even though I can't stop wiggling sometimes), and I know that pulling on the leash doesn't get me very far and my walk ends sooner, so I'm doing really well with reminders here and there.

I love settling into my kennel quietly with my kong stuffed with a tablespoon of canned puppy food.

I really want to find my forever family where I don't have to share so much of the attention with everyone else! I want to be the best boy ever for you!

Events at public spaces with too many other dogs and things going on are really overwhelming to me, so adoption days are hard for me to attend right now. Please put in an application to adopt me and we can meet in a calmer place.

Meet ten of the smartest, sweetest little pups you'll ever cross paths with! Rescued from the Rosebud Reservation when they were just four weeks old, this resilient litter has spent the last few weeks blossoming into brave, affectionate, and well-rounded puppies. Featuring a mix of Shepherd, Husky, and three uniquely gorgeous brindle coats, this crew has the looks and the brains to match! They’ve been raised around kids, cats, and adult dogs, making them super adaptable and great at reading the room.

Because of their smart and active lineage, these pups will thrive best with families who enjoy keeping their dogs mentally engaged and physically active. They are classic puppies in every way: eager for attention, a little bit mouthy while they learn what’s a toy and what isn't, and completely obsessed with giving warm puppy snuggles. They’ve overcome a tough beginning and are so ready for their next chapter—could your home be the missing piece?

214952315.description:
** This is a courtesy post for the owner. Do NOT submit an application. Please email the owner with inquiries or interest at: Mariah.wilson1@icloud.com **

Hi! My name is Wednesday, and yes, I am just as cute and quirky as my name suggests.

I’m a Great Dane; however, I’m told I’m no ordinary Great Dane. I’m what they call a pocket Great Dane because I am only 93lbs and likely won’t get much bigger. I do still firmly believe I’m the perfect size for your lap, though. Personal space? Never heard of her.

I’m 2 years old, and I have a whole lot of love to give to the right person. And underneath all these long legs is a goofy, loving girl who really just wants to be with her people. Once you’re one of my people, I want to be wherever you are. Sitting on the couch? I’m coming. Going to another room for 30 seconds? Seems suspicious, but I’ll probably follow you. Working from home? Perfect; I happen to have extensive experience as a work-from-home supervisor.

A Few Important Wednesday Facts

1. First, I take bedtime very seriously.

I sleep in my kennel at night and genuinely do well there, but there is one requirement: please cover me with my blanket. Yes, physically tuck me in; I like to be cozy!

2. If you’re the type of person who wants an enormous dog cuddling with you in bed, though, I am also VERY willing to discuss alternative sleeping arrangements. I will happily snuggle up with you and take my job as a giant heated blanket extremely seriously.

3. I also get the zoomies. Like BIG zoomies! One minute, I am flying around like someone just informed me that I’m actually a greyhound. Five minutes later? Absolutely exhausted. Must sleep immediately.

4. I love my toys, being with my humans, getting attention, cuddling, being cozy, and generally participating in whatever my family is doing. I'm a big personality in an even bigger body, and life with me definitely isn't boring.

The Home I’m Looking For

As much as my family loves talking about all of my silly qualities, they also want to be completely honest about the things I need.

My dream family would have experience with dogs, and bonus points if you know and love Great Danes or other giant breeds! I need someone who understands that loving me also means continuing to work with me, respecting my boundaries, and helping me be the best version of myself.

I do have a few things I need my future family to understand about me. Sometimes I have a hard time sharing my space and resources with other dogs. I’ve shown resource-guarding and territorial behaviors with the dog I currently live with. Because my family loves me very much and wants me to be successful, they think I would be happiest as the only dog in my new home. Honestly, being the center of attention sounds pretty good to me anyway!

I LOVE children, but sometimes forget how big I am. If our family has children, please be patient as I learn to live with my littlest friends! I will thrive in an environment with people who understand my boundaries and can give me structure.

Right now, I get to stay home with Mom all day, and if I were making the rules, I’d really love for that to continue in my new home. I love having my person around, even if we’re just hanging out doing our own things.

That doesn’t mean you can never leave me, though! I’m kennel trained and actually sleep in my kennel every night. If I need to be kenneled during the workday, I can do that too, but I’ll need some good exercise and attention before you leave and again around lunchtime. A giant girl has to stretch her legs!

And there’s a pretty good reason my family recommends kenneling me when nobody is home… Sometimes I make questionable decisions when I’m bored.

I’m young, smart, curious, and occasionally a little mischievous. Leaving me unsupervised with too much freedom can result in me finding my own entertainment, and apparently humans don’t always appreciate my creative choices. So, until we know I can be trusted, my kennel is the safest place for me when I’m home alone.

I’ll Bring My Stuff!

Don't worry, I'm not showing up empty-pawed.

My family wants my transition to be as comfortable as possible, so I’ll be bringing a bunch of familiar things with me, including my kennel, bed, blanket, Vault food container, one bag of my current food, my vitamins, and some of my favorite toys.

That means I’ll have familiar smells, familiar food, my favorite things, and, most importantly, the blanket you are now contractually obligated to cover me with at bedtime.

My Family Is Going to Be Picky

My current family isn't looking for just anywhere for me to go. They love me tremendously, so they're going to be pretty picky about who gets to be my next family (especially Mom, if I’m being honest with you). You'll need to fill out an application, provide references, share a little about where I'll be living, and come meet me at least twice. Basically, we're going to date before we make things official!

And there's one really important promise you'll have to make: if life ever changes and you can't keep me, you’ll reach out to my first family. Always. I will never be surrendered to a shelter, given away, sold, or passed along to someone else.

I know I'm not the right dog for every home.

I need someone who understands that sometimes the best dogs aren't necessarily the easiest dogs. I need structure. I need someone willing to understand my boundaries. I need exercise and stimulation so I don't start brainstorming unauthorized home-improvement projects. I need my blanket tucked around me when I sleep, obviously.

But in return? You get me!

A giant, goofy, blanket-loving, zoomie-having, professional cuddler who will happily spend her days hanging out with you and then act like we've been separated for six years when you come back from checking the mail.

My family loves me enough to wait for the right person. So if you're looking for a giant best friend, have room in your home and your heart for a girl like me, I'd really love to meet you.

Love,

Wednesday

Meet Snickerdoodle, an Oklahoma girl turned Midwest sweetheart. She's a goofy, snuggly little pup with plenty of puppy energy and an endless amount of love to give. Snickerdoodle gets along with kids, cats, and other dogs. She loves giving her favorite feline friends approximately one million kisses. Seriously, this girl LOVES cats! She'll wiggle her way right over to them and shower them with kisses. She's still learning to read other animals' social cues and understand when they want space, but her intentions are always to love or play.

She's already showing off her smarts by knowing how to sit and lay down! Like any young pup, she still has some puppy habits to work through. She's working on potty training and learning appropriate play manners. When she gets tired, she can become a little mouthy, but she redirects fairly well when offered a toy.

One of Snickerdoodle's most adorable quirks is her voice! Her barks and whines are more like little squeaks, earning her the household nickname "Squeaker." She is currently still finding her voice, so a home without shared walls may be the best fit.

Snickerdoodle is looking for a family who understands the joys (and occasional chaos!) of puppyhood and is willing to give her the patience, consistency, and guidance she needs to grow into an amazing companion.

If you're looking for a playful, affectionate, goofy pup who will keep you laughing and make sure everyone gets their fair share of kisses, Snickerdoodle could be your girl!

214963666.description:
Meet Sweetie! Her name says it all! Sweetie is an absolutely beautiful silver-colored girl with a heart just as sweet as her name. She has the perfect combination of a gentle, affectionate personality and an adventurous spirit.

Sweetie is incredibly sweet and gentle. She's often the first to approach you, looking for attention and affection. And when you pick her up, get ready for the sweetest little surprise! She loves to rest her head over your shoulder and wrap her little paws around you for what feels like a hug. She's a natural snuggle bug and absolutely loves being close to her people.

But don't let all those cuddles fool you—Sweetie is also the biggest adventurer of the bunch! She's often off exploring different parts of the yard on her own, confidently taking in everything around her. One of her favorite things to do is wander around the garden, investigating all the interesting sights and smells. She loves being part of the action and is always ready for her next little adventure. She has been wonderful around the two young children in her foster home.

She and her siblings are working on potty training and are already doing a great job consistently using potty pads both in their pen and when they're out exploring.

Sweetie is the best of both worlds—a gentle, affectionate cuddle bug who also loves exploring and discovering the world around her. She's looking for a family who will give her plenty of love, snuggles, and opportunities for adventure as she grows.

If you're looking for a sweet companion who will greet you with a hug and happily join you on your next adventure, Sweetie might just be your girl!

Could this beautiful girl be your newest family member?

Marshall is a handsome all-brown puppy with the sweetest personality.

Of the four siblings, Marshall is currently the most laid-back and easygoing. He loves staying close to his people and is always happy to soak up some extra attention and snuggles. If there's a lap available, Marshall would be more than happy to claim it!

Although we've only had a short time to get to know him, it's been so fun watching his confidence blossom each day. He's becoming more adventurous, exploring a little more, and showing us new sides of his personality as he settles into his foster home.

Marshall has been introduced to our backyard and enjoys getting outside to explore. He's also been doing well around the two young children in his foster home.

Could this sweet boy be your newest family member?

Meet Tumbleweed! Don't let his name fool you... this little guy isn't blowing through life in a hurry! Tumbleweed is a sweetheart who prefers to take life at a slower pace. He's a little shy at first, but underneath that timid exterior is a friendly, playful boy just waiting to blossom in his forever home.

Tumbleweed is already showing off some pretty impressive life skills! He's crate trained, mostly potty trained, and sleeps quietly in his kennel all night long. He's a calm, quiet kind of guy who doesn't need to be the center of attention to make your day better.

He enjoys the company of other dogs and is wonderfully respectful of his furry friends. Toys bring out his playful puppy side, too! He hasn't been introduced to cats or children in his foster home, but given his gentle, easygoing personality, we think he has the potential to fit right in with a family that includes either.

Tumbleweed may take a little time to come out of his shell, but with some patience, love, and encouragement, we think he'll really take root.

If you're looking for a sweet, easygoing companion who will bring a little sunshine (and just a touch of tumbleweed) into your life, this boy might be the perfect addition to your family!

Harlow was hit by a car before coming into Rescue Network. She is currently recovering at her foster home from a pelvic fracture, but doing very well. She is now able to walk around a bit to get what she needs (water, food, toys, etc.), and to go to the door to go potty. She still needs to be lifted up and down the steps, and onto or off of the couch. She prefers to lay at your feet above all else.

She does not like everything super soft, though, and sometimes likes the cool of the kitchen floor.

Once she has recovered, her real personality will be able to shine. You can tell she really wants to play with the other dogs already, but isn't allowed to yet.

I'm the perfect mix of playful and cuddly. I love my toys, especially anything I can tug on or chew, and I'm always up for making new dog friends! I've met dogs of different sizes and think they're all potential playmates. I'm still learning my puppy boundaries and manners, but I'm working on it!

When playtime is over, I turn into a cuddle bug. One of my favorite things is snuggling up next to my humans when I'm ready for a nap. I'm also a pretty great car passenger and enjoy going along for the ride!

I'm still working on my potty and kennel training, but I'm making great progress with potty training. I've only had a couple of accidents so far! Being left alone isn't my favorite thing just yet, but I'm learning and will need a family willing to help me build confidence and independence.

I haven't met cats or other animals yet, and I haven't been around children, so those introductions will be new for me.

I'm looking for a family who will give me patience as I grow, plenty of toys to play with, lots of adventures to experience, and, most importantly, a cozy spot to cuddle up when I'm sleepy.

I may only have three legs, but I have a whole lot of love to give. Could you be my furever family?

Abbey is a sweet, gentle 7 year old Great Pyr mix who spent her life in Arkansas until her owner passed away. Since she's been thru several traumatic transitions, we want to make sure this sweet girl finds the right forever home.

1. Abbey absolutely loves her people and needs someone home more than not.

2. Abbey will do best as an only dog, but could live with another low energy senior dog. Abbey does not appreciate young, high energy dogs.

3. Abbey does all her business outside and even lets us know when she needs to go outside by giving a paw paw on the door.

4. Because of her breed, Abbey needs a fenced yard to keep her safe, and does not care for being left outside alone without her people.

5. Abbey walks well on a leash for walks, but is not a candidate for dog parks and needs slow leashed intros to strange dogs.

6. Abbey sleeps quietly all night in our bedroom.

7. Abbey has a big bark but only uses it occasionally, so because of that and her size, she's not a good fit for apartment living.

8. Abbey takes treats by our hand very gently.

9. Abbey knows basic commands like sit, down and come.

Abbey has been a very loved indoor dog her whole life. She’s house-trained, wonderful with kids and is good with other low energy dogs and prefers a quiet, peaceful home. She also loves a good car ride, so she’s ready to be someone’s co-pilot.

Dusty’s journey is nothing short of an absolute transformation. Dusty has blossomed into a healthy, confident, and vibrant puppy!

Beyond her resilient spirit, Dusty is a true head-turner. She has the most unique, beautiful eyes that seem to change color—sometimes looking green, and other times a warm straw color.

This lively girl has officially discovered the joy of being a puppy! Dusty loves wrestling with her brother, Rusty, and running around with the other dogs in her foster home. She has recently unlocked a love for toys—especially if you are willing to play a good game of tug-of-war with her, chewing on hooves, and chomping on Himalayan yaks milk chews.

But don't let her playful sass fool you; once playtime is over, Dusty switches right into cuddle mode. She is a snuggler of epic proportions and will gladly curl up right next to you (or on you) to recharge.

Dusty is incredibly bright and catching onto house manners fast. She is doing fantastic with her potty training, already knows her name, understands the "go potty" command, and has even started ringing the bells on the door when she needs to head outside.

Dusty is highly adaptable and would do wonderful in just about any home that is ready for the fun, energy, and commitment of raising a puppy. If you have room in your heart and your couch for a resilient, loving, and slightly sassy companion, Dusty is ready to meet you!

214849584.description:
Meet Rusty! This resilient, sweet little guy is searching for his forever home, and his transformation is nothing short of amazing.

When Rusty first arrived from a South Dakota reservation on October 5th, he was a very frail, timid little boy bravely battling a case of mange. Fast forward just a few short weeks, and he has completely blossomed! Thanks to a lot of love and care, Rusty is now a healthy, vibrant puppy. His beautiful fur is growing back in, and he is sporting a very nice, healthy coat.

Rusty is a gentle soul who can still be a bit shy at times. He is an observer first, usually letting his sister, Dusty, take the lead in new situations. But once he watches from the sidelines and realizes everything is safe, he is ready to join in the fun! Because of his early struggles with mange, his feet get cold easily, so he isn't the biggest fan of cold weather or rain. Wet grass is a no-go for this little gentleman, but he absolutely loves playing outside when the weather is beautiful. Plus, he has discovered that wearing a nice, warm doggy coat makes outdoor adventures much more cozy!

When it's playtime, Rusty loves romping around with his sister and the resident dogs in his foster home. He is an expert toy tester and loves chewing on hooves, Himalayan bones, and checking out an assortment of fun toys.

Rusty is also proving to be a very smart boy. He already knows his name, is doing fantastic with his potty training, and understands exactly what to do when you tell him it’s time to go potty. When night falls, he is an angel in his kennel, where he currently curls up to sleep with his sister. While he would always prefer to be right next to his humans and might give a tiny whine for the first few minutes, he quickly settles himself down and drifts right off to dreamland.

Rusty will make a wonderful addition to almost any family. If you are ready to give him plenty of love and help him continue building his confidence, Rusty is ready to fill your life with puppy kisses!

214978633.description:
Harlie is a sweet, middle aged (in cat years), gray girlie who was under socialized as a kitten and then spent her formative years in the care of a lovely elderly woman. Unfortunately, when the woman could no longer take care of Harlie, she found herself in a loud shelter environment where she wasn't thriving.

Thankfully, her foster happened to have an open cat space for her to decompress in and she is coming back out of her shell. She currently spends most of her day finding a quiet space to spend her time in, but will come out to say hi to the foster family when they are in the same area.

She takes her time getting to know a space, before she can get to know the person. But she really loves to boop her head against your hand once she is confident enough she is space, to ask for love.

Harlie will most likely do best in a home where the "vibes are chill". And she is the "main pet" aka most likely the only cat or dog but we don't think she'd object to their being lizards or fish.

215011552.description:
Milo is a little man who loves with his whole heart and his whole wiggly body. When this boy wags his tail, everything wags.

Milo's previous family loved him, but grooming wasn't their strong suit. He came to us after a much-needed shave to get rid of painful mats, so he's rocking a bit of a "work in progress" look right now. Don't let the haircut fool you: underneath is one handsome, happy pup.

What he's like at home:

• Smart and eager to learn. He's still working on potty training. We think that's mostly from adjusting to a new home and maybe never having been taught, and he's a quick study.

• Crate trained. He sleeps and spends the day in his crate. He'll let out a few loud protests and then settles within a minute or two. Once potty training clicks, we think he'd do great roaming free.

• A grazer. He doesn't eat all his food at once, so free-feeding may work well for him.

• Goofy, snuggly, and toy-loving. He has a medium energy level, so he's happy to play and just as happy to curl up with you afterward.

• Great with chaos. In his foster home he lives with two 8-week-old puppies who climb all over him, a 70 lb, 2-year-old dog named Kota who is obsessed with him, and two kiddos (ages 3 and 5). He takes it all in stride. When he's had enough, he lets you know with a bark or by chasing the pest away.

Milo is without a doubt going to be an amazing BFF. Maybe that's you!

Adoption fee includes spay/neuter, all age-appropriate vaccinations (distemper, rabies, and bordetella), heartworm and flea/tick preventatives, heartworm test (dogs over 9 months), FIV/FeLV test (cats - one in the litter), dewormed, and microchip implant (including registration).

Rescue Network is strictly foster based which means all adoptable animals are in a home and there cannot be a meet until an application is submitted and approved. We have no way of knowing the breeds in the animals. All breeds listed are best guess.
